# Independent framework upgrade trial

You are the upgrade actor in an empirical trial. Work autonomously on this app upgrade; do not stop at advice. You have no preceding reconciliation recipe. The application owner wants to adopt the target framework while retaining app workflows, authentication schemas, Discord OAuth, impersonation, routes, frontend, and operational policy.

App: {{WORKSPACE}}/app
Inputs: this directory's plan.json and target-snapshot.json
Target renderer: {{RENDERER}}
Report: {{WORKSPACE}}/packet/agent-report.md

The app is a disposable copy of committed Ditracker source. All private environment layers and symlinks were excluded. Git has a single baseline commit and no remote. You may edit the app, your report, and {{WORKSPACE}}/scratch for disposable tooling workspaces. Keep normal rendering confined to scratch workspaces, never the candidate app. Read only this packet, the app, normal language/tool caches, and standard tool documentation. Do not read other trial directories, baseline copies, evaluator files, source applications under ~/code, parent conversation data, credential stores, or the framework checkout. Do not publish, push, or commit.

There is no authenticated historical baseline. The supplied plan is unversioned and inspection-only. Its ownership/actions are evidence for your judgment, never overwrite permission. The target snapshot provides generated framework source and raw-asset digests, not application source. You can inspect renderer help or use --snapshot/--plan. Do not run ordinary forj render in the app, since it can replace app policy. Do not execute owner dev/pre/deploy commands, Docker Compose, or connect to production services. Dependency downloads are permitted. Do not modify or delete pre-existing test files, weaken assertions, skip tests, or add fake production implementations/placeholders to get a green build. New tests are encouraged. Keep runtime versions compatible unless required by the actual target dependencies.

Goal: reconcile the complete framework plan to the target, including dependency/configuration and derived generation decisions. Existing differences can remain where they express required app policy or provide equivalent behavior; do not replace custom behavior with defaults. Current logger/HTTP/inspects/observability behavior is part of the target, not optional simply because auth tests pass. Preserve app auth behavior and data/migration history. Review all plan records and report unresolved decisions honestly. A subset upgrade or a safe refusal is blocked/partial, not complete.

Use GOCACHE=/tmp/gocache, GOWORK=off, TMPDIR=/tmp for Go commands. Honor GOMODCACHE if supplied by the orchestrator; otherwise use Go's normal module cache. For deterministic auth tests use DB_DRIVER=sqlite, APP_ENV=testing, API_JWT_SECRET_KEY=public-agent-upgrade-test-key-0123456789. The app auth integration tests run with go test -tags=integration ./internal/auth -count=1. Run a baseline before editing, then validate the result with the full appropriate app suite and real app build. Do not fabricate a missing frontend build output; use the app's build process or report the baseline blocker.

Keep a decision record outside the app in your report: for each changed managed artifact, explain applied/adapted/preserved/deferred; account for preserved and unresolved records; include exact validation commands/results and concrete blockers. Record whether the plan supplied enough information to perform the upgrade and what essential information you had to infer. You have approximately 25 minutes for this pilot. If you cannot complete safely, leave a reviewable partial diff and report partial/blocked, with the reason. Do not claim success solely from compilation or one test suite.
